items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: Because they have stuff from James Brown, they had stuff from Elvis Presley, they had jazz guys, they had a lot of, you know ownership of tunes.

ctx.x: Oh. Now that was a civilized way to resolve that situation.

Well you’re fighting, what good is it going to do? You know what I mean? It just doesn’t make any sense at all. And then I’ve had a couple of — I had to learn the business of music on the fly because my stepmother basically controlled everything until she died. So © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

then my brother and I took it over, and I said well let’s put an LLC together. So we put an LLC and we structured it a couple of ways. We structured it first of all that the ownership would be 51-49. So I would be the 51 part and he would be the 49 part. He didn’t really like that but what that did for me was allow me to be able to do anything with anybody anywhere without having to contact him to get his permission, so I can make deals. And then we split the royalties 50-50. Well I ended up suing one company…
